claims.text: reaping is a separate act, run by whoever knows the attempt is fully resolved.
claims.why: The method is public and documented as separate; no auto-reap occurs in this chunk.

claims.text: 1. THIS manager object allocated it, in THIS process (:attr:`_allocations`, written by :meth:`create_worktree`), its worktree has been through :meth:`cleanup_worktree`, and its tip is byte-identical to the sha this manager itself read from git at allocation time.
claims.why: Checks allocation.get('worktree_removed') and compares tip to allocation.get('branch_tip_at_creation').

claims.text: 2. Some OTHER ref still contains that tip, so deleting the branch orphans no commit.
a branch leaked by a CRASHED run is never reaped, because the process that could vouch for it is gone.
claims.why: Only in-memory _allocations are examined; on-disk records are reported unverifiable and never acted on.

claims.text: Returns: One dict per allocation examined, with ``branch``, ``action`` (``deleted`` / ``retained`` / ``absent`` / ``pending`` / ``unverifiable``) and ``reason``.
claims.why: Every branch in the loop appends a dict with those keys; unverifiable rows are appended from _report_unverifiable_records.

claims.text: Raises: RuntimeError: If any branch that was cleared for deletion could not be deleted. Every allocation is still examined first; the failures are reported together rather than aborting on the first one.
claims.why: Failures are collected in `failures` list; loop continues; RuntimeError raised after loop with joined messages.

claims.text: Reported rather than ignored so the leak is visible; reported WITHOUT any field parsed out of the file, because every byte in it is candidate-writable and echoing a forged branch name back at an operator as though it meant something is how the previous version printed false reasons.
claims.why: Rows contain branch=None, path=None, record=filename only; no parsed content.

claims.text: Refs OTHER than ``refs/heads/<excluding>`` whose history holds ``sha``.
claims.why: Uses for-each-ref --contains, filters out the excluded ref case-insensitively.

claims.text: A FAILED CALL IS NOT AN ANSWER. ... Deleting the ``except`` below lets the ``RuntimeError`` escape ``reap_branches`` instead of retaining; that mutation SURVIVED the suite until 2026-07-28, and it is killed now by ``test_reap_retains_a_branch_when_git_cannot_say_who_contains_its_tip``.
claims.why: except RuntimeError returns [] which retains the branch; the test name is referenced but not in this chunk.

claims.text: Compared case-INSENSITIVELY although git refs are case-sensitive: the only effect of a spurious match is that a ref is dropped from the holder list, which retains the branch.
claims.why: Uses casefold() on both sides; a spurious casefold match removes a holder, making holders potentially empty and retaining.

claims.text: Delete a branch already PROVEN to hold nothing but its base commit.
claims.why: Only called after reap_branches verified tip and holders; -D only after re-verifying tip.

claims.text: ``-d`` is tried first so git's own merged-check applies. If git refuses anyway ... the sha proof (re-taken here, so the branch cannot have moved in between) is what authorises ``-D``.
claims.why: Tries -d, on RuntimeError re-reads tip and compares to proven_tip before -D.

claims.text: The path is proven to be an allocated worktree first: a swapped directory would otherwise turn ``git add -A`` + ``git commit`` into a commit of the developer's working tree.
Return whether the candidate worktree differs from its HEAD.
claims.why: Returns bool of git status --porcelain output; empty output means no changes.

observations.what: The docstring for reap_branches claims that the worktree has been through cleanup_worktree, but the code only checks allocation.get('worktree_removed') which is set by cleanup_worktree; no direct verification that cleanup_worktree ran in this chunk.
The claim about a test name (test_reap_retains_a_branch_when_git_cannot_say_who_contains_its_tip) is uncheckable in this chunk; the test is not present.
_refs_containing returns [] on any RuntimeError, which includes cases like git missing or repo locked; this is fail-closed but means the branch is retained even if the git failure is transient.
_delete_unused_branch falls back to force-delete after re-verifying tip; the re-verification uses git rev-parse which could theoretically race again, but the window is narrow.
commit_candidate and has_changes both call _require_allocated_worktree which is not defined in this chunk; its behavior is uncheckable here.
